A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. They describe the same dual-expert grounding framework and SCOUT dataset, despite the change from LynX to TWIST & SCOUT and extensive reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization, grounding, image-understanding, dataset-quality, and ablation results in Sections 4–5 and the appendix.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds component, backbone, and biomedical domain-shift experiments in Section 5.

M1.justification: The renamed framework retains the frozen image-understanding MoE, trainable grounding MoE, learned alpha fusion, stepwise loss, and BERT-based inference routing. The LLaVA backbone experiment tests the existing framework; expanded SCOUT generation explanations do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: v2 adds biomedical VQA-RAD evaluation alongside general visual question answering. It removes v1's multi-object evaluations on PVOC and LVIS under Protocols 1–2, while retaining their single-object localization evaluations. RefCOCO variants and Flickr30k Entities remain covered in Appendix Table A.4.

E2.justification: v2 adds Grounding DINO and Ferret-7B to the REC and grounded-captioning comparisons, and adds OpenFlamingo with LoRA to the localization comparison. I-80B's image-understanding results disappear from the corresponding benchmark table, although its parameter information remains in the appendix.

E3.justification: v1's CogVLM-reference Common Class and Class Grouping protocols are removed. v2 centers grounded-captioning evaluation on sentence-transformer class mapping against COCO annotations, corresponding to v1's Protocol 3. New experimental designs include joint biomedical/general-VQA training, a LLaVA backbone, and a single-expert configuration.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls separating TWIST, SCOUT, and stepwise-loss contributions; an alpha-gating intervention; backbone transfer; and biomedical domain-shift analysis. The expert-count ablation gains a one-expert control, and dataset ablations are revised. Negative-supervision analysis is retained in Appendix A.1 rather than removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The existing 100-sample dataset-quality assessment remains a point-estimate comparison.

E6.justification: The COCO-annotation comparison reports 14.0 AP, 48.3 AP50, and 17.3 APL in v1 Table 2 versus 15.0, 49.3, and 19.1 in v2 Table A.3. Numerous REC and ablation entries are revised, added, or removed; these revisions do not establish controlled performance gains across versions. The zebra example changes from an irrelevant textual answer to coordinates. Existing localization and seven-benchmark image-understanding scores are retained.

T1.justification: The MoE, transformer, expert-fusion, training-loss, stepwise-loss, and inference equations remain mathematically equivalent despite reordering and renumbering. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central claims of learning grounding without forgetting and using synthetic stepwise supervision remain. v2 narrows the evaluation contribution from a pipeline operating at multiple granularities to a grounded-captioning protocol, and drops v1's explicit state-of-the-art localization claim from the conclusion.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations involving alpha-mediated feature reuse, backbone generality, and resistance to biomedical domain shift. It attributes scaling saturation to CogVLM's limited objects per image, rather than only describing a plateau. The existing limitation that SCOUT quality depends on CogVLM is retained and relocated.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents the 512k SCOUT default, exclusion of 6,549 RefCOCO validation/test images from COCO training, and the IoU threshold used in the existing human quality assessment. It also promises code release. v1's explicit 0–99 coordinate-encoding description disappears. These disclosures do not establish changed underlying settings, reruns, or actual code availability.

R1.justification: The positioning around fine-tuning versus extensive pretraining and the comparison with PIN remain. v2 expands the contrast with LoRA and object detectors, adds Grounding DINO, Ferret, Sentence-BERT, and newer multimodal-model references, and removes several earlier citations.

P1.justification: The main text is extensively rewritten and reorganized. LynX becomes TWIST & SCOUT, VLM terminology largely becomes MLLM, SCOUT receives a separate section, stepwise training moves into the framework description, and ablations become part of the experiments section.

P2.justification: v2 adopts two-column formatting, redesigns Figures 1–2, adds a data-generation diagram, and restructures tables with color highlighting and combined comparisons. Full grounding results move to the appendix, and retained examples and prompts are redistributed across pages. These changes substantially exceed renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 better supports the framework through explicit component and gating controls, backbone testing, and stronger comparators. Clearer figures and newly documented evaluation details also improve assessability. The gain is limited by reduced cross-dataset grounded-captioning evidence and insufficient reconciliation of revised scores and their training conditions; higher reported values alone do not demonstrate improvement.
